question_en:
I am organizing display support materials for historical gowns in a costume museum. Please answer the following based on the attachment:

1. What are the name, object number, design house, and holding institution of this gown?
2. In the open collection of this institution, find all ball gowns by the same design house, limited to those that are in the public domain, have an official main image, and have an accession year no later than that of the gown shown in the image. Examine each main image one by one, and select gowns that show a frontal view with both mannequin arms exposed at least from the elbow to the wrist. List their date, object number, accession number, and material.

Response format: Answer in points numbered (1)–(2). Answer question 1 in text. For question 2, list all matching gowns item by item in a table with columns for date, object number, accession number, and material.
answer:
(1) Name: Ball gown; Object number: 156027; Design house: House of Worth; Holding institution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art.

(2)

gold_trajectory:
# Detailed Simulated Search Trajectory · 8-3-G01

## Step 01 · Locate the museum object using the gown's overall silhouette and pattern

Action: Extract the silhouette and fabric decoration from the main body of the gown retained in the current input to perform an image search. Example query: Met House of Worth Ball gown 1898 rhinestones.

Evidence observation: The corresponding object is Met object 156027; the official main image can verify the same gown, whereas the background work scene is not part of the museum identity. The title Ball gown is the object name, and 156027 is the objectID; do not concatenate numbers like 2009.300 from the accession number to form the object number.

Evidence links:
https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/156027
https://collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/objects/156027
https://images.metmuseum.org/CRDImages/ci/original/DP-1028-001.jpg

Result of this step: Establish the correspondence between the input object, the design house, and the museum record.

## Step 02 · Read identity and accession year threshold from the object API

Action: Read the title/objectName, artistRole, artistDisplayName, accessionYear, and institutional information from the JSON for 156027.

Evidence observation: objectName=Ball gown; artistRole=Design House; artistDisplayName=House of Worth; accessionYear=2009; isPublicDomain=true and primaryImage is not empty. The holding institution is The Metropolitan Museum of Art. The accession year upper limit in the question is 2009, not the work's production year 1898.

Evidence links:
https://collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/objects/156027
https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/156027

Result of this step: Determine the four identity items for Question 1 and the subsequent time threshold.

## Step 03 · Switch from restricted web paths to available official API evidence

Action: Check the fields provided by the object page and the API materials respectively, and retain the web address as an entry point for manual review.

Evidence observation: Seven saved direct object web requests returned a 429 Vercel challenge page on 2026-08-10; material or date cannot be read from these challenge pages. The authoritative fields available in the question package come from the official Collection API JSON, and image addresses come from primaryImage; this also explains why both the API and the object page are provided for each subsequent item.

Evidence links:
https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/156027
https://collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/objects/156027

Result of this step: Continue evidence collection using the API, rather than treating failed pages as successful scrapes.

## Step 04 · Query a broad candidate pool and fix 140 IDs

Action: Query within the costume department (departmentId=8) with House of Worth ball gown and hasImages=true, retaining the complete objectIDs.

Evidence observation: The archived search returned 140 IDs. Matching vague keywords in the search does not equal satisfying the question's conditions; the results may include other clothing types, other design houses, non-public domain objects, or objects without a main image. Each object's fields must be read individually before filtering.

Evidence links:
https://collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/search?hasImages=true&departmentId=8&q=House%20of%20Worth%20ball%20gown

Result of this step: Obtain a broad candidate pool of 140 items pending verification.

## Step 05 · Convert the question's scope into explicit field filters

Action: For each of the 140 IDs, read the official JSON and check the clothing name, design house role and name, public domain status, non-empty main image, and accession year.

Evidence observation: Retention conditions are objectName=Ball gown, artistRole=Design House, artistDisplayName=House of Worth, isPublicDomain=true, primaryImage not empty, and accessionYear≤2009. The work's production date does not replace accessionYear; the hasImages search condition itself does not guarantee the presence of the primaryImage used in the question prompt.

Evidence links:
https://collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/search?hasImages=true&departmentId=8&q=House%20of%20Worth%20ball%20gown
https://collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/objects/156027

Result of this step: Only after field filtering is the closed set requiring individual image inspection established.

Action: Check the object ID, status, and failed fields row by row according to the full candidate review table saved on 2026-09-29; open the corresponding API when specific values need to be verified.
